name: demo_facturas
description:
Supplier invoices addressed to iberclean Parts, S.L., for the non-Teccom flow. Each document is a commercial invoice for automotive parts and accessories, emitted by a Spanish or European supplier and received via email.

The target ERP (Microgest) expects a JSON with three header sections and a line-items array. Extract the fields listed below so the conversion layer can assemble the final payload.

IMPORTANT TERMINOLOGY (changed in v1):
In this schema, "client" / "cliente" refers to the SUPPLIER (the entity that ISSUED the invoice — the party Iberclean is paying), NOT the recipient. Iberclean is the buyer/recipient on every invoice in this corpus, so its data is constant and not extracted. Every `*_cliente` field (nombre_cliente, razonsocial_cliente, direccion_cliente, poblacion_cliente, provincia_cliente) holds SUPPLIER data — name, legal name, street, city, province of the issuer. Treat the `cif` / `razonsocial` and `*_cliente` blocks as two views of the SAME entity (the supplier); razonsocial_cliente will typically be identical to razonsocial.

Extract two groups of fields:
1. Header — a single set of values per invoice covering: supplier identity (cif, razonsocial AND the *_cliente block), invoice identity, financial totals (with up to 3 VAT tranches), eco-taxes, discounts, shipping, and payment details.
2. Line items (lineas) — one entry per physical line in the invoice body. Lines may be grouped by delivery note (albaran) that appears as a sub-header above a block of rows: when that happens, replicate the albaran value on every line of the group.

CRITICAL — Supplier CIF vs. Iberclean CIF:
The invoice shows TWO tax IDs: one for the SUPPLIER (issuer) and one for IBERCLEAN (recipient). You MUST extract the SUPPLIER's CIF into the 'cif' field. Iberclean's CIF (B99887766, possibly printed with an ES prefix as ESB99887766) appears in the recipient/'Bill to'/'Destinatario'/'Customer' block. NEVER put Iberclean's CIF in the 'cif' field.

CREDIT NOTES / ABONOS — sign convention:
Some documents in this corpus are credit notes (abonos / facturas rectificativas), not regular invoices. When the document IS a credit note:
- ALL monetary header fields (total, ibruto, portes, tnfu, tsigaus, tgases, idto) MUST be negative (or zero).
- ALL line-level importe values MUST be negative.
- cantidad stays positive; the sign lives in importe.
- VAT percentages and dto1..dto5 remain positive (they are rates/percentages).

fields.name: total
fields.description:
Grand total of the invoice INCLUDING VAT and all taxes/surcharges. This is the final 'Total a pagar' / 'Total factura' / 'TOTAL EUR' — usually the largest, most prominent figure at the bottom. Use a dot as decimal separator, no currency symbol.
Sanity check: total MUST be strictly greater than ibruto for standard invoices (because it includes VAT). If total ≈ ibruto, you have probably extracted the base imponible by mistake — look for the larger figure that includes the VAT amount. Common confusion: the 'Base imponible' or 'Subtotal' line is NOT the total — the total is below the VAT lines.

fields.name: ibruto
fields.description: Total invoice amount before VAT — the sum of all taxable bases. Labels: 'Base imponible', 'Subtotal', 'Total sin IVA', 'Importe neto', 'Net amount'. If the invoice has multiple VAT tranches, this is their sum (base1 + base2 + base3).

fields.name: portes
fields.description: Freight or shipping charges as printed in the invoice's totals/summary section, VAT excluded. Labels: 'Portes', 'Gastos de envio', 'Transporte', 'Shipping', 'Carriage'. Extract the value shown in the summary; default 0 if none is printed. Credit notes: negative if the credit includes freight.

fields.name: tnfu
fields.description: NFU eco-tax for tyre recycling ('Tasa NFU', 'Ecotasa neumáticos') as printed in the invoice's totals/summary section. Default 0 if not present in the summary.

fields.name: tsigaus
fields.description: SIGAUS eco-tax for used oil management ('Tasa SIGAUS', 'SIGAUS') as printed in the invoice's totals/summary section. Appears on invoices for lubricants and oil-containing parts. Default 0 if not present in the summary.

fields.name: tgases
fields.description: Fluorinated gases tax ('Impuesto gases fluorados', 'Tasa gases') as printed in the invoice's totals/summary section. Appears on invoices for air conditioning components or refrigerants. Default 0 if not present in the summary.

fields.name: idto
fields.description:
Total discount amount applied to the invoice, expressed as an amount in euros. If only a discount percentage is shown (e.g. 'DISCOUNT % 5,00'), multiply it by the total merchandise amount to compute the euro value. Look in the invoice summary/totals section (usually at the bottom). Default 0."

Scope rule: idto is ONLY for discounts that apply to the ENTIRE invoice. If a discount applies to a subset of lines (a single line, a single albarán block, a product group), it belongs in dto1..dto5 on those specific lines, NOT in idto. Examples: per-albarán discount ("Dto 5% sobre albarán 109452") → dto1=5 on lines of that albarán. Per-line discount column → dto1 on each line. Invoice-wide "Rappel 3% sobre total factura" → idto.
This field captures global discounts that are NOT broken down per line. There are three patterns:
Pattern A — Lump-sum discount after the lines table (DOLZ / TOTALENERGIES style): the supplier lists all lines at full price (no per-line discount columns), then shows a single discount row or block AFTER the lines table, before the VAT summary. Labels: Descuento total, Dto. global, Rappel, Descuento comercial, Bonificación. Extract the discount AMOUNT here. Since the per-line importe values are the full (undiscounted) price, the conversion layer will use idto to adjust the base. Do NOT also back-calculate dto1 on each line — that would double-count. The printed Base imponible in these invoices is already reduced by the discount.

Pattern A2 — Discount rows inside the items table, at the end (Exide style): the discount rows appear INSIDE the items table, after the last product lines, as rows with a description and a negative NETO/importe but NO referencia, NO cantidad, NO precio unitario. Labels: RAPPEL ESPECIAL SOBRE (*), DESCUENTO GARANTIAS SOBRE (+), Rappel s/ventas, Dto. financiero. There may be multiple discount rows — sum their absolute values into idto. These rows are NOT line items (they have no product identity) — the lineas extraction skips them. The SUMA Y SIGUE / SUMA TOTAL on the invoice reflects the gross line sum; the final Base imponible is reduced by these discounts.

Pattern B — Cascading percentages in the header (Liqui Moly style): the invoice header shows Desconto Comercial 2,00% / Desconto Adicional 2,00%. In this case, the discount is captured per-line (dto1, dto2 on every line), NOT here. Set idto = 0.

How to distinguish: if the discount is shown as a percentage that should apply to every line → per-line dto1/dto2 (Pattern B, idto=0). If the discount is shown as a lump-sum euro amount, either after the lines table (Pattern A) or as negative-amount rows inside the table with no product data (Pattern A2) → idto.

Do NOT fill from per-line discount totals or from a 'sum of discounts' informational column.

Credit notes: negative if the credit note reverses a discount.

fields.name: lineas
fields.description:
Every line item on this page. Return ALL rows, omit none, invent none.

**You see one page per call.** Rows at the top of the page with no group sub-header above them continue the block opened on the previous page; when that block matters, you are told about it in the context. Starting a new page is not a reason to start a new group, and those rows must not be left with empty group fields.

### Grouping

Most invoices split their lines into delivery blocks. The block's identifier is printed ONCE, on a row of its own that interrupts the table, and governs every row below it until the next one. Recognise it by its **structural role, not by its label**: a row that spans the table width, carries no value in the amount columns, and separates two runs of line items. Suppliers call it «Albarán», «Delivery N.», «Order no.», or something else entirely.

Column variant: if there are no separator rows but a column holds the same value across a run of consecutive rows and then changes, that column is what groups them.

Propagate the block's identifier and its date to **every** row in the block. A row that falls inside an active block never carries them empty. Do not invent a new identifier for a row that has no sub-header of its own above it.

### Rows that are NOT line items

Subtotals and carried-forward rows («Suma anterior», «Suma y sigue», «A transportar»), page totals, per-block subtotals, the tax summary (base imponible, IVA, total factura), column headers repeated on each page, the group separator rows themselves, customs or tariff summary tables — rows whose identifier is a 6-10 digit numeric code with amount, weight and piece columns — product-family summary tables, which carry only a description and an amount with no reference, quantity or price, and legal text, signatures or address blocks.

When in doubt the test is: a line item has a reference or a description **and** a quantity **and** a price. A row carrying only an amount is a total.

### Rows that ARE line items

Freight and eco-tax rows when they occupy their own row inside the table with their columns filled. Surcharges. Credits and returns, keeping the amount negative. Core or casco deposits. And rows whose reference is blank but which carry a description and an amount: the blank reference is deliberate, leave it null.

These rows belong to the active block like any other.

### Wrapped descriptions

A long description may span two or three visual lines of one logical row. Join them into one: with a single space when the break falls between words, with no separator when it cuts mid-word. Keep characters exactly as printed, even where they look like encoding artefacts.

### Check before you answer

Every line must satisfy `cantidad × precio × (1 − dto1/100) × (1 − dto2/100) = importe`, within one cent. If it does not, there is a discount you missed: look for a narrow percentage column, a compound notation such as «10/5/2», a negative amount on a separate row, or a discount announced at block level.

If the discount exists but its percentage is printed nowhere, leave `dto1` and `dto2` at 0 and keep `importe` exactly as printed. **Do not back-calculate a percentage the document does not state.**

### Number conventions

Decimal separator is the dot, no currency symbol. Discounts are percentages (`15`, `72.73`), not fractions. In three-decimal price columns, drop trailing zeros. Mind the Spanish thousands separator: a quantity printed `1.110` is the integer 1110, not 1.11 — check it against the unit of measure and the row's amount.

# CRITICAL
The purchase order's validity is independent of the delivery-note (albaran) identifier: a block may open a new albaran and continue under the same purchase order. A new albaran never ends the current purchase order — only a new purchase-order reference does. When the first lines of a page carry no purchase-order reference of their own, they keep the one carried over from the previous page, even if their albaran is new. Never take the next purchase-order reference that appears further down the page.

nested_fields.name: albaran
nested_fields.description:
Identifier of the delivery block this line belongs to: whatever the invoice uses to group consecutive lines, under any label («Albarán», «Delivery N.», «Order no.», «Nota de entrega»…). How the block is detected and propagated is described on the `lineas` field; what matters here is which value to store.

Keep the format exactly as printed, with prefixes, leading zeros and separators: `ALB-20260401`, `A/2026/00123`, `VALB/26-008249`, `2026ALB0031931`, `OUT_1/2026`, `1091/2026`, `1-000790`, `4000249`, `812191`, `109498`, `5622`. If it comes compounded with a position and a date (`81071620/000010 04.02.2026`), store only the identifier. If the block's sub-header shows the long form (`2026ALB0031931`) and a per-line column shows a short one (`31931`), store the long form.

**It is never the invoice number.** If a candidate is identical on every line of the document and appears in each page's header, it is the invoice number: do not use it. A real delivery-note number changes at least once across the invoice, unless the whole invoice covers a single delivery.

Also never the albaran: agent or customer codes (`AGENTE 145`, `Nº Cliente 34465`), registry or RPP codes (`NEU/2021/000000377`), or the recipient's own order reference (`S/PEDIDO`, `Su pedido`, `Your order n.`, `Nº Pedido Cliente`) when it appears alongside a separate grouping identifier — there the order reference is metadata and belongs in `npedido`.

When the block's sub-header carries several identifiers: if one is explicitly labelled as a delivery note, that one wins, even if it is a short 3-4 digit integer. Only when none is labelled, prefer the alphanumeric or structured one (carrying a year, prefix or separator) over a bare integer.

null only if the invoice has no grouping identifier of any kind — no separator row, no grouping column. This is uncommon: exhaust the possibilities before concluding it, and never fall back to the invoice number.

nested_fields.name: fechaalb
nested_fields.description:
fechaalb

Date of the delivery block this line belongs to, in YYYY-MM-DD. It is normally printed inside the block's sub-header row, tied to the identifier by a label or a preposition: 'Fecha:', 'DE FECHA:', 'fecha', 'de', 'of', 'dd.', or simply as a date token sitting next to the identifier. Examples: `Albaran - 4000249 - 17/09/2024 - …`, `****** ALBARAN: 109452 DE FECHA: 03/02/2026 ******`, `Order no. 812191 of 9/02/2024`, `Albarán: VALB/26-008249  Fecha: 20/02/2026`, `Albarán 2026ALB0031931 fecha 01/04/2026`. It travels with the block exactly like the identifier does; propagation is described on the `lineas` field.

**Never fall back to the invoice issue date.** If the block has no date of its own, leave this null.

When several dates appear in the same sub-header, take the one structurally tied to the grouping identifier — not a secondary purchase-order or operation date. In particular, a date attached to the recipient's order reference (`Your order n.: 120618 dd. 9/02/2024`, `S/PEDIDO … Fecha …`) is the order's date, not the block's, even when the two rows sit next to each other.

null only when the invoice genuinely carries no per-block date, which is uncommon.

nested_fields.name: npedido
nested_fields.description: The invoice recipient's purchase order number (número de pedido) for the goods on this line or albaran group. This is the recipient's own reference, which the supplier prints on the invoice to identify the order — it is NOT the albaran number and NOT the invoice number. It typically appears in or near the albaran sub-header row, with labels like 'S/PEDIDO', 'Pedido', 'Num. Pedido', 'VTRO. PEDIDO Nº', 'NÚM. PEDIDO', 'ORDER N.º', 'PRESUPUESTO B2B', or embedded at the end of an albaran sub-header line. The value is usually a 6-digit number (e.g. '162338', '161819') but may occasionally have a letter prefix or different length. Extract the identifier exactly as printed. Return null if no purchase order number is visible for this line's albaran group.

nested_fields.name: referencia
nested_fields.description: Supplier's part reference / SKU / catalogue code for the item on the line (the supplier's own code, not the recipient's internal code). Labels: 'Referencia', 'Ref', 'Cod', 'Codigo', 'Articulo', 'Art', 'SKU', 'Part number', 'P/N', 'Material', 'Item ref. number', 'Référence'. Preserve case, hyphens, slashes and dots exactly (e.g. 'FIL-OIL-1234', '0 986 221 001', 'W712/95', 'REC181986-203', 'IDLTRB-012SP3'). If the line shows both the supplier's reference and an OEM cross-reference, prefer the supplier's own reference. If the codigo wraps to two visual lines, concatenate them with no separator before extracting.

nested_fields.name: descripcion
nested_fields.description: Commercial description of the article as printed on the line (e.g. 'CORREA DISTRIBUCION GATES', 'FILTRO ACEITE MANN'). If the description wraps across several visual rows, concatenate them into a single string separated by spaces. Do not embed reference, quantity, price or discount values in this field. If the line cell uses a 'Albaran: X - Material NAME con referencia REF' formatting (Renault-dealer style), strip the 'Albaran:' prefix and the 'con referencia REF' suffix and keep only NAME.

nested_fields.name: cantidad
nested_fields.description: Number of units billed on the line. Labels: 'Cant', 'Cantidad', 'Uds', 'Qty', 'Unidades', 'Quantity'. Use a dot as decimal separator. Ignore the unit-of-measure column ('UD', 'KG', 'LT', 'M', 'UN'). If quantity-ordered / quantity-served / quantity-billed columns appear separately, extract the billed one. Always positive, even for credit notes (the sign lives in importe).

nested_fields.name: precio
nested_fields.description: Unit price before discounts and before VAT. Labels: 'Precio', 'P. unit', 'Precio unitario', 'P/U', 'Unit price', 'PVP', 'P.Tarifa', 'P.S/IMPTO', 'Precio ud.', 'Pr. Unitario', 'Net Price', 'Prc.Neto'. Dot decimal separator, no currency symbol. If the supplier shows gross and net unit prices in separate columns, extract the gross one — discounts go in dto1..dto5. If the price is per 100 or per 1000, normalise to price per single unit. Always positive, even for credit notes.

nested_fields.name: importe
nested_fields.description:
Net final amount of the line, VAT excluded, after all discounts. Labels: 'Importe', 'Total', 'Total linea', 'Neto', 'Subtotal', 'Precio Neto', 'Amount', 'IMP. NETO', 'Valor', 'Montant'. Dot decimal separator, no currency symbol. If the supplier only shows a VAT-included amount, extract the best available value.

Sign convention: preserve the sign as printed. Negative values are valid for refund/credit lines and for credit notes (abonos). If the entire document is a credit note but the supplier prints line amounts as positive, NEGATE them — see the CREDIT NOTES section in the root description.
CRITICAL: always extract the importe value exactly as printed on the invoice. NEVER recalculate it by applying discounts, taxes, or any other adjustment. If the printed value is the gross amount (before discount), extract the gross amount. If the printed value is the net amount (after discount), extract the net amount. The importe field is a faithful transcription of what the invoice shows.

nested_fields.name: dto1
nested_fields.description: First-level discount applied to the line, expressed as a percentage (e.g. 5, 10.5 — not 0.05). Labels: 'Dto', 'Dto 1', '%Dto', '% DTO', 'Descuento', 'Disc', 'Desc.'. If the supplier packs multiple discounts into a single cell with a separator ('10/5/2', '10+5+2'), the FIRST value goes here and the rest go into dto2..dto5. IMPORTANT: make an extra effort to detect and extract discounts from visible table columns even when the column label is ambiguous. Many invoices show a '%D' or 'Dto' column that is easy to miss. Do NOT apply discounts from header or footer text that are not part of the line items table — those belong in the header-level idto field. If there is no discount, return 0 (not null). Always positive (it is a percentage).

nodes.prompt_hint:
You are parsing commercial supplier invoices addressed to a single automotive-parts distributor. These are multi-page PDF invoices (often 1–60+ pages, up to 800+ line items) from dozens of different European suppliers. Your job is to convert every visual element into faithful, well-structured HTML tables so a downstream extractor can read them accurately. ## Table structure — be surgical Each PDF page may contain several distinct visual blocks. Parse EACH block as its own with a descriptive id attribute. Common block types: - **Issuer block** (supplier logo, name, address, CIF/NIF, phone, email) — top-left or top-center. Tag: `
`. This is the SUPPLIER's identity. **In v1, the extractor pulls BOTH `razonsocial` AND the entire `*_cliente` block from this single table** — getting it parsed cleanly is more important than ever. - **Issuer footer / fiscal block** — many suppliers print their CIF, mercantile registry, and full legal address ONLY in the page footer (Picoya, Racing Oil, Alfaro Brakes, Terre Power). When the header has only a logo + email, you MUST parse the footer fiscal text as `
` so the extractor can find the CIF and confirm the legal name. - **Customer block** (the recipient's name, address, CIF, customer code) — usually labelled 'Cliente', 'Bill to', 'Destinatario', 'Ship to', 'Customer'. Tag: `
`. This is the recipient. In v1 the extractor IGNORES this block for `*_cliente` fields, but parsing it correctly still matters: it's used to disambiguate the supplier CIF (so the extractor knows which CIF NOT to pick). - **Invoice header** (invoice number, date, series, due date, PO reference) — near the top. Tag: `
`. - **Line items table** — the main body with columns for reference, description, quantity, price, discount(s), amount. Tag: `
` where N is the page number. - **Albaran / delivery-note sub-header rows** — these interrupt the line-items flow. They are NOT data rows. CRITICAL: preserve these EXACTLY as they appear — as a full-width row (``) WITHIN the line items table, NOT as a separate table. The extractor needs to see them inline to propagate the albaran ID to subsequent lines. - **VAT summary** (base imponible, IVA rate, IVA amount, totals) — usually near the bottom of the last content page. Tag: `
…
`. - **Payment info** (bank, IBAN, payment terms, vencimientos) — footer area. Tag: `
`. - **Eco-tax block** (NFU, SIGAUS, gases fluorados) — sometimes a small separate table or a section within the VAT summary. Tag: `
` if separate. ## Issuer info — be especially clean Because v1 reuses the issuer block for the `*_cliente` fields, parse it with these guarantees: - One `` per logical line (name, street, postal+city, province, phone, email, CIF). - If the postal code, city, and province are on the same printed line (`17401-Arbúcies (Girona)`, `08191 Rubi - Barcelona - Spain`, `46134 Valencia (Valencia)`), keep them in ONE ` ``` Recognise sub-headers by ANY of these surface forms: - `****** ALBARAN: DE FECHA: ******` - `Albaran - - - - ` - `Albarán: Num. Pedido Clt/Web: Fecha: ` - `Num. alb.: Codigo: Fecha: ` - `Albarán fecha ` - `ALB N.º de ` - `Albarán: ` Whichever form appears, ALWAYS: 1. Use a single `` outside the main line_items table. The extractor will skip it. ## Inline freight and eco-tax LINE ITEMS — parse as ordinary rows Some suppliers bill freight and eco-taxes as line items inside the items table (NOT in the totals strip). Examples: - Picoya: a row with `referencia="P"`, `descripcion="PORTES (SE CARGARAN EN FACTURA)"`, qty 1, importe = freight cost. - Racing Oil: rows with `referencia="SIGAUS"` (Spanish industrial-oil management fee) or `referencia="GENCI"` (plastic-packaging tax). - Terre Power: a row with empty `referencia` cell, `descripcion="transporte urgente pagados"`, only the `Importe` column filled. Parse these as REGULAR `` rows in `line_items_page_N`. Specifically: - If a cell within the row is genuinely BLANK on the printed page (e.g. blank Cantidad / Precio for an inline transport row), emit `` — do NOT fabricate a value. - Preserve the row's position relative to the surrounding albaran block — these inline lines inherit the active albaran. ## Column alignment — the core challenge Automotive invoice tables often have 8–14 columns with narrow numeric fields. Misaligned columns cascade into extraction errors. Apply these rules: 1. **Right-align numeric columns mentally.** Quantities, prices, discounts, and amounts are right-aligned in the source. When OCR or layout analysis is ambiguous about which column a number belongs to, check: does the number make sense as a quantity? a price? a discount percentage? Use the column header AND the surrounding rows to resolve ambiguity. 2. **Discount columns are easily missed or merged.** They may be narrow (just `%D` or `Dto`), may contain no value for some rows (blank = 0%), or may pack multiple cascading discounts into one cell separated by `/` or `+`. Parse them as they visually appear — if it's one column, it's one `` rows for wrapped description text. 5. **Use rowspan/colspan faithfully.** If a cell visually spans multiple rows or columns, reflect that with the appropriate HTML attributes. Albaran sub-header rows ALWAYS use `colspan` to span all columns. ## Series consistency — the tiebreaker When vertical alignment is ambiguous (a number could belong to the column on its left or its right), apply the SERIES CONSISTENCY heuristic: look at the values in the same column in the rows above and below. Numbers in a column tend to have similar magnitude and format. A `72.73` is more likely a discount percentage than a quantity if the surrounding rows in that column also show values like `71.84`, `66.56`. Similarly, `1.0` looks like a quantity column if the rows above show `1.0`, `2.0`, `1.0`. ## Two distinct fiscal entities — keep tables separate Every invoice has data for TWO legal entities: 1. **The SUPPLIER (issuer):** name, CIF, address, registration. Header letterhead and/or footer fiscal text. 2. **The RECIPIENT:** name, CIF, address, supplier-side customer code. Usually in a 'Cliente' / 'Bill to' / 'Customer' box. Parse these into SEPARATE tables with distinct IDs. NEVER merge issuer and customer data into a single table — the extractor relies on the table ID to know which CIF is the supplier's (RULE #1) and which entity to populate the v1 `*_cliente` block from (RULE #0). If the supplier's CIF appears in a footer legal text block (e.g. `Inscrita en el Registro Mercantil de... CIF: A12345678`), still parse it as a row in `issuer_info` or a dedicated `
` so the extractor can split — do NOT shred them across cells. - If the supplier letterhead has the brand commercial name AND a separate legal name (e.g. logo `RACING OIL` + footer `RACING OIL S.L.`), parse BOTH and keep them tied to the same issuer entity via consistent table IDs (`issuer_info` for header, `issuer_legal` for footer). The extractor will use the commercial form for `nombre_cliente` and the legal form for `razonsocial` / `razonsocial_cliente`. - When the only place the CIF appears is the footer legal text (e.g. `Inscrita en el Registro Mercantil de … C.I.F. B-NN.NNN.NNN`), parse that sentence as a row in `issuer_legal` — DO NOT drop it as "boilerplate". ## Albaran sub-headers — the highest-impact parsing decision Albaran sub-header rows interrupt the line table and announce a new delivery-note grouping. Parse them as full-width rows inside the line-items table: ```html
****** ALBARAN: 109452 DE FECHA: 03/02/2026 ******
` spanning all data columns of the line table — never break the row across cells. 2. Apply `class="albaran_header"` so the extractor can identify it programmatically. 3. Place it INLINE between the line rows it governs, NOT as a separate table. 4. Preserve the FULL ID as printed (with prefix, year, leading zeros, slashes/dashes) — even if the line table's left-hand `Alb. Nu.` column shows a short form. DO NOT: - Convert the sub-header into a regular data row. - Lift the sub-header into a separate `` above the line items. - Drop the date next to the albaran (the extractor needs both ID and date in the same row). - Confuse it with a `S/PEDIDO` / `Su pedido` / `Doc Origen` / `S./Referencia` row — those are customer purchase references, NOT albaranes. Tag those as `` so the extractor knows to skip them. ## Page continuations Multi-page invoices repeat the column header row at the top of each page. Parse each page's line-items block as a separate table (`line_items_page_1`, `line_items_page_2`, etc.) with its own ``. This helps the extractor track page boundaries. Watch for these page-break artifacts: - **`Suma anterior` / `Carried forward` / `A transportar`** — running-total rows, NOT product lines. Tag: ``. - **Repeated column headers** — parse as `...` for each page's table. - **Footer totals on intermediate pages** — tag: ``. - **`Suma y sigue`** at end of intermediate pages — tag: ``. - **CRITICAL — albaran continuity**: when an albaran block spans a page break (no closing sub-header on page N, no opening sub-header on page N+1), DO NOT inject a synthetic albaran row at the top of page N+1. Leave the line-items table headerless and let the extractor inherit the previous page's active albaran. Adding a fake row would corrupt the propagation logic. ## Customs / HS-tariff summary rows — DO NOT confuse with line items Some export-style invoices (Alfaro Brakes pattern) print a single row above the line-items table that aggregates all lines for customs purposes: ``` Quant. | Description | Tariff nom. code | Origin | Amount 229 BRAKE PADS 870830 SPAIN 2.362,42 ``` This row's `Amount` equals the sum of every real line below it. If parsed as a normal row, the extractor will double-count. Tag it as a separate table or row class so it's clearly distinct: ```html
229BRAKE PADS870830SPAIN2.362,42
``` Or inline as `
`; if there are 2–5 separate Dto columns, give each its own ``.
